question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{arsinh}⁡2{x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡2{x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{(2{x}^{2})}^{2}+1}}\cdot {(2{x}^{2})}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{4{x}^{4}+1}}\cdot 4x \\  & =\frac{x}{\sqrt{4{x}^{4}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
